kind_note: A standard gen_configs.py / run_experiments.py / merge_experiments.py TLSF repair campaign driven end to end by scripts/campaign.py. The only factor is run_weakening, carried as the `weakening` directory factor (wkon/wkoff) rather than as a sweep, because sweep J is absent from gen_configs.TLSF_SWEEPS and only the --weakening crossing reaches the TLSF grid. Both arms of a (spec, seed) pair run on the same host. The filter is a final screen that draws nothing from the RandomSource, so the two arms of a pair search bit-identically and differ only in what survives step 6.
question: Whether run_weakening_filter, which keeps only repairs the original logically implies, forecloses reachable repairs on the TLSF arbiter families. An audit found the restriction enforced in exactly one place: the mutation operators already produce incomparable candidates freely (mutate_atom_name draws a replacement atom uniformly from the declared alphabet), the per-generation chain never consults the original's semantics, the maximality filter keeps antichains, and the realizability gate never references the original. Of 431k archived result rows, zero carried weakening = wkoff for any arbiter-family specification.
decision: The restriction costs reachable repairs. 9 of 120 (spec, seed) pairs yielded under wkoff and not under wkon, 0 the other way; McNemar exact one-sided p = 0.00195. By family: lily02 5, arbiter 3, prioritized-arbiter 1, with arbiter-aurus, arbiter-handshake and full-arbiter tied at 20/20. Repair counts 250 against 403. The wkoff-only repairs are substitutions rather than deletions on inspection, which was the outcome the plan's threats section named as the one that would have voided the finding: lily02 swaps the atom `go` for `grant` in G(cancel -> X(!grant U go)); prioritized-arbiter flips two polarities, turns an && into <->, and swaps g_m for g_1, with ASSUME/ASSERT/GUARANTEE counts unchanged at 1/7/4; arbiter adds an assumption and rewrites G F g0 into X(g0 W X g1). This is evidence for demoting run_weakening from a filter to a reported tag. It is not evidence that the repairs are correct: the fitness objectives still under-price deletion, so incomparable does not mean right.
decision_rule: None was pre-registered, deliberately. PLAN.md section 8 sets out why: the campaign is a reachability probe, and no prior was sharp enough to name a threshold. The endpoint, its pairing and the direction counting as an effect were all registered before any row was collected. Read the decision above as a judgement on registered evidence, not as a rule firing.

corpus_cut.when: 2026-08-19, after 24 rows and before any endpoint was read
corpus_cut.why: The cost model in PLAN.md section 5 came from 2026-08-10-arbiter-probe, which predates MRS status grading as the shipped default (1.89x cost) and p_remove_guarantee. Per-run cost on this binary is ~6x the prediction: full-arbiter 65.5 s against 10.8 s, and amba hit the 900 s cap in both arms on every attempt, recording n_repairs = 0 while taking ~88% of the wall time. round-robin-arbiter, simple-arbiter and load-balancer went on cost alone, all three already yielding under wkon. Carried as a phase-level `specs` override in campaign.toml, so the profile still states the corpus the question is about. PLAN.md section 10 is the record.
corpus_cut.cost_to_the_claim: The campaign cannot say the restriction is free across the arbiter corpus, only across the six families it covers. No family was removed on the basis of what its arms showed.

premise_superseded: PLAN.md sections 1 and 2 frame the question around families yielding close to nothing, citing arbiter-probe's full-arbiter at 1/40 and prioritized-arbiter at 0/40. On this binary those families are 20/20 and 18/20 under wkon. Same cause as the cost model failure. The registered endpoint in section 4 is the paired yield difference and never referenced the zero-yield baseline, so it is unaffected; only the motivation is stale. PLAN.md section 11 is the record.

reproduction_note: Regenerate the configs with `python3 scripts/gen_configs.py --tlsf --weakening both --sweeps A --levels gen10 --out-dir experiments/configs-wkarb` at 864ae63. The configs themselves are not archived: experiments/ is gitignored by content and the two emitted files differ in exactly one line, run_weakening. Note that gen_configs emits a key only where a sweep overrides it, so everything else comes from the binary's defaults at 864ae63.
known_caveats: The wkoff arm was scored by fitness objectives that under-price deletion: Logarithmic containment saturates (src/fitness/semantic_similarity.cpp:35-45), a tombstoned requirement contributes a flat 0 to the semantic fold (:228-231), and status_score_mrs normalises by the candidate's own live guarantee count (src/fitness/status.cpp:263-265). The arm is read for reachability, never for repair quality. PLAN.md section 7.

run_weakening is a final screen, so every wkoff repair was reachable under the current search all along and was discarded at output. The campaign measures what the filter discards, not what a search freed from the restriction would find.

The first launch of this campaign produced no rows at all: campaign.py embeds a campaign's `build` verbatim as `if ! @BUILD@ > "$buildlog" 2>&1; then`, and shell `!` binds to the first pipeline of an AND-list, so a compound build ran cmake, short-circuited gen_configs away, and still reported the stage a success. Fixed for this campaign in 80c2790 by wrapping the pair in sh -c. campaign.py itself is unfixed as of this close.
